title: Shared local update-rule basis with rule Views
hypothesis: A shared rank-3 local-kernel basis and task codes preserve heldout cellular-rule update/rollout behavior with at least 25% fewer complete bytes than independent rules and improve on scalar FiLM.
mirror_coordinate: per-rule coefficient vector selecting a shared kernel basis
logical_multiplicity: 24 local cellular dynamics from one shared basis

development.selection_metric: heldout one-step nRMSE, 12-step rollout nRMSE, state norm ratio, complete bytes, MAC proxy

fresh.reason: synthetic aligned kernel mechanism screen; no audit opened after exact native basis alias

success_gate: Heldout update and rollout nRMSE <=0.02, max state norm ratio <=1.1, >=25% complete-byte savings vs independent, and strict Pareto gain over native factorization and FiLM.
failure_gate: Quality/byte/compute gate miss or exact native kernel-factorization payload/function alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
amendments: A01 during development: removed elementwise clipping of generated kernels, which had broken the preregistered rank-3 teacher structure. The initial off-family output is preserved separately and excluded.

A02 during development: after the corrected 24-rule bank achieved only 19% serialized-byte savings, increased the rule bank to 96 tasks (64 train/32 heldout) to test amortized complete serialization overhead. Rank, seed, scoring and gates were not changed; corrected 24-rule results remain preserved in RESULTS_DEV_24TASKS.csv.
boundaries: Synthetic scalar-field recurrent convolution rules only; kernels are generated from a shared rank-3 basis.
No trained growing/regenerating NCA, multi-channel morphology, biological task, or hardware runtime claim.
Training-free oracle aligned mechanism screen; no capacity claim.
